Team capacity report for one person and week
Sample wording: adapt it to your country's law and your own practice.

The contract hours are {col:cap.contract}. The company is closed on {col:cap.hol_days} days and the person is on leave for {col:cap.leave_days} days, so the person can work {col:cap.work_days} days, which is {col:cap.avail_h} hours.
The allocated hours are {col:cap.alloc_h}, which leaves {col:cap.free_h} free hours. The load of the week is {col:cap.load} and the load check shows: {col:cap.state}.

A person above {set:over_pct} of the available hours needs work moved to somebody else. A person below {set:free_pct} can take new work. The project manager and the PMO lead agree any change in the weekly resource meeting.
Monthly utilisation statement for one person
The capacity of the month was {col:util.capacity} hours. The person logged {col:util.hours} hours on projects, of which {col:util.billable} hours were billable and {col:util.nonbill} hours were not.
Utilisation was {col:util.util} against a target of {col:util.target}, a gap of {col:util.gap}. The check shows: {col:util.state}. The billable share of the hours logged was {col:util.share}.
The hours cost {col:util.cost} and the billable hours have a charge value of {col:util.value}.
We use this statement in the monthly review with the PMO lead. A low utilisation is first a question about the work planned for the person, not about the person.
Timesheet summary of a project for a client invoice

Up to today the team logged {col:projects.hours_logged} hours on this project, of which {col:projects.billable_h} hours are billable. The charge value of the billable hours is {col:projects.billable_value}.
The labour cost of all hours is {col:projects.labour_cost} and contractors cost {col:projects.contractor_cost}. The budget of the project is {col:projects.budget}.
Today {col:projects.team_now} people are allocated to the project for {col:projects.hours_alloc} hours a week, and {col:projects.contractors} contractors are booked.
The hours come from approved weekly timesheets. Please send any question about a line to the project manager before we issue the invoice.
Leave note for the team calendar
The leave runs from {col:leave.start} to {col:leave.end}, which is {col:leave.days} working days. Company closure days are not counted.
Approved by {col:leave.approved_by}. Cover: {col:leave.cover}. The cover check shows: {col:leave.clash}.
Please put this leave in the team calendar and tell the project managers whose projects the person works on. Of these days, {col:leave.days_30} fall in the next 30 days.

Project: {col:projects.name} ({col:projects.code}), status {col:projects.status}. Project manager: {col:projects.manager}. Dates: {col:projects.start} to {col:projects.end}, forecast end {col:projects.forecast_end}.
{col:projects.team_now} people are allocated now for {col:projects.hours_alloc} hours a week, and {col:projects.contractors} contractors are also booked.

So far the project used {col:projects.hours_logged} hours, with a labour cost of {col:projects.labour_cost} and {col:projects.contractor_cost} for contractors, against a budget of {col:projects.budget}.
Open skill gaps and resource requests of the project are on the Skill Needs and Resource Gaps sheets. The project manager reviews them in the weekly resource meeting.

We confirm your booking from {col:bookings.start} to {col:bookings.end}, {col:bookings.weeks} weeks at {col:bookings.hours_week} hours a week. The rate is {col:bookings.rate} per hour and the planned cost is {col:bookings.cost}.
Please send your hours every Monday for the week before. We pay the hours that match your timesheets and this booking.
Please confirm this booking by return message. Any change of hours or dates needs our agreement first.
The person worked {col:overtime.hours} overtime hours. The approver is {col:overtime.approved_by} and the status is {col:overtime.status}.
The cost per hour is {col:overtime.rate}. With the premium of {set:ot_premium} the cost of the overtime is {col:overtime.cost}.
Overtime is agreed before it is worked. Time off or payment follows the policy of the company. Overtime on the same project week after week is a sign that the plan needs more people.
Skills matrix report of one person
{col:staff.skills_n} skills are recorded with an average level of {col:staff.avg_level} out of 5.
The person is allocated {col:staff.alloc_now} of the week on {col:staff.projects_n} projects and has {col:staff.free_hours} free hours a week.
Levels run from 1 (learning) to 5 (can teach others). The full list with the date of every check is on the Skills Matrix sheet. A rating older than {set:skill_days} days should be checked again.
Team allocation summary for the managing director

The person is allocated {col:load.alloc} of the week ({col:load.alloc_h} of {col:load.hours_wk} hours) on {col:load.projects_n} projects, with {col:load.free_h} hours free. In the last four weeks the person logged {col:load.logged_wk} hours a week. The load check shows: {col:load.state}.
We share this summary with the managing director when a person is above {set:over_pct} or below {set:free_pct} of the week, so that hiring, contractor and priority decisions rest on the same facts.

Open Start and type your company name and your own limits in the yellow cells: the allocation above which a person is over, the share that counts as full or free, the overtime premium and the days a timesheet may be late.
Fill Team with each person: role, team, cost per hour, charge rate, weekly hours, utilisation target and main project manager. Allocation now, free hours and skills fill in by themselves.
List your projects on Projects and your contractor vendors on Vendors. Record every skill of every person on Skills Matrix, and the skills each project needs on Skill Needs.
Enter who works on which project on Allocations: the share of the week and the dates. Hours per week, the state and the phones fill in. Use Roll-ons and Roll-offs for every change.
Add the company closure days on Company Holidays and record leave on Leave. Weekly Capacity then shows the hours really available for the next weeks against the hours allocated.

Enter the weekly hours of each person on Timesheets and the dates submitted and approved on Timesheet Approvals. The sheet marks every week as approved, waiting, returned or missing, with the days late.
Fill Utilisation by Month from the closed timesheets and read it against the target of each person. Use Load Check in the weekly resource meeting to see who is over, full, balanced or free.
Book contractors on Contractor Bookings, log their weekly hours on Contractor Timesheets and compare them with the hours on their invoices before you pay.
Record open requests for a role or skill on Resource Gaps, overtime on Overtime Log, courses on Training and the rates of each role on Rate Card.

Use the 14 calculators for weekly capacity, utilisation, allocation, staffing hours, leave cover, overtime, blended rate, contractor or employee, booking cost, hiring, levelling, timesheets, a lost day and what-if.
Print 10 sheets and 9 reports and letters, follow 9 checklists and tap a message link to open a chat with the text ready.
Read Team and Time Dashboard and Charts every week: people over 100%, free hours, missing timesheets, utilisation, leave, overtime and contractor cost.
Delete the demo rows when you are ready and type your own. Every calculated column, figure and chart then works with your data.
Control project budget, cost, purchasing and billing in one workbook
Control project budget, forecast, purchasing and client billing
Forecast at completion with CPI and SPI
percent complete, planned percent and actual cost give earned value, both indexes, the estimate to complete and the final cost of every project
planned, earned and actual cost to date for every project and month show the month when cost or schedule first slipped
Three-way match of order, receipt and invoice
each vendor invoice is checked against the order and the goods received and flagged before you approve it for payment
Quote scoring with your own weights
price, lead time and quality are scored out of 100 with the weights you set, ranked inside each request and checked against the vendor chosen
Budget by category with transfers and draws
the budget of every project and category moves with approved transfers and reserve draws, and shows spent, open orders and what is left
every draw on a project reserve shows the reserve planned, drawn to date, left and a warning before the reserve is used up
Client billing with due dates and days late
payment milestones and change orders get a due date from the client terms, a state, days late and the amount outstanding
each change request shows extra cost, extra days, price to the client, margin and a warning for a margin below your target or a late decision
Accruals with cut-off and reversal month
work done and not yet invoiced is listed by month with the cut-off date, the month it reverses and a flag for stale accruals
Spend plan against actual by month
the planned spend of each project and month is set against what was spent, with the cumulative plan and a check against your amber limit
Order delivery and late order warnings
orders show goods received, last delivery, value still open and a warning when goods are late or only part delivered
Vendor record with days to pay and disputes
every vendor shows spend, open orders, unpaid invoices, average days to pay, overdue and disputed invoices

Projects: budget, price, dates and money position
One row per project with budget, contract price, dates and percent done; approved changes, budget now, spent, billed, paid and the cost forecast fill in by themselves.
Cost categories: budget and spend of each category
One row per cost category; budget now across all projects, spent, left, share of all spending and a check fill in from the budgets and cost lines.
Vendors: terms, spend, orders, invoices and payment record
One row per vendor with service, terms and contact; spend, open orders, invoiced, outstanding, average days to pay, overdue and disputed invoices fill in by themselves.
Project budgets by cost category with moves and spend
One row for each project and cost category with the approved budget; moves, approved changes, budget now, spent, open orders, what is left and a check fill in by themselves.
Phase budgets: budget and spend of each work phase
One row for each project and work phase with the approved budget; spent in that phase, what is left, the share of the project budget and a check fill in by themselves.
Cost lines: every cost by project, category and vendor
One row per cost with date, project, category, vendor and amount; month, group, age, the project manager phone and a check for approvals waiting too long fill in by themselves.
Spend plan: what each project planned to spend in each month
One row per project and month with the planned spend; actual spend, the difference, cumulative plan and actual and a check against your amber limit fill in by themselves.
Forecast at completion: earned value, CPI, SPI, final cost
One row per project; type only known extra cost. Percent complete, planned percent, actual cost, earned value, CPI, SPI, estimate at completion, variance and reserve fill in by themselves.
Known extra cost not yet booked
Earned value by month: planned, earned and actual cost
One row per project and month with the percent complete at month end; earned value, planned value, actual cost to date, CPI, SPI and the money of each month fill in by themselves.
Purchase requests: what to buy and where it stands
One row per request with project, vendor, item, amount and need date; days waiting, quotes received, best price, chosen vendor, order number, the vendor phone and a check fill in by themselves.
Quotes: vendor offers scored on price, lead time and quality
One row per quote; the score weighs price against the lowest offer, lead time against the fastest and quality, using your weights. Rank in the request, validity and the verdict fill in.
Purchase orders: amount, tax, goods received, open value
One row per order; tax, total, goods received, last delivery date, invoiced, delivery state, three-way match and the value still open fill in by themselves from receipts and invoices.
Receipts: goods and services received against each order
One row per delivery against an order; vendor, project, order amount, total received, the vendor phone and whether the delivery is complete fill in by themselves.
Vendor invoices: due dates, payment and order match
One row per vendor invoice; due date from the vendor terms, days to pay, payment state and the match against the order and the goods received fill in by themselves.
Change costs: extra cost, days, price and margin
One row per change request with extra cost, extra days and the price to the client; margin, margin share, days waiting, the contact phones and a check against your margin target fill in.
Client billing: milestones, change orders, collected
One row per payment milestone or change order of a client project (internal projects have none); due date from the client terms, state, days late and amount outstanding fill in by themselves.
Contingency log: draws on a project reserve
One row per draw on a project reserve with the category that receives the money; reserve planned, drawn to date, left, share used and a check fill in by themselves.
Budget transfers: money moved between categories
One row per transfer with the category it leaves and the category it joins; approved transfers change the budget by category. The sponsor phone and a check that the source can pay fill in.
Accruals: work done but not yet invoiced, month by month
One row per accrual with month, project, vendor and amount; the cut-off date, the month it reverses, the project manager and finance phones and a stale-accrual check fill in by themselves.
Expense claims: what team members claim
One row per expense claim with person, project, date and amount; the month, the age, the project manager and a check for claims waiting too long or returned fill in by themselves.

Estimate at completion by four methods

Method 1: actual cost plus the rest at budget rate
Method 3: actual cost plus the rest at CPI times SPI
